author: @FrankCurzio
text:
It looks like the AI layoff boom has started to backfire.

I was just going through a Reuters investigation on Meta, and holy shit...

They drew up plans to cut some teams by as much as 60% and let AI agents do the work. THEN Zuckerberg called off the next round of layoffs hours before the first one even started.

And when you look at the numbers... they tell you why.

Engineers were pushing out 220% more code, BUT major technical and security incidents jumped 40%.

So people spent 70% more time putting out fires.

AI cranked out way more work, and humans spent way more time cleaning it up.

A different report I saw this week showed something similar.

32% of hiring managers said they brought back the exact jobs they cut for AI.

Think about how dumb that is. You fire people, pay a fortune for AI, then pay again to hire the same people back.

Look, I’m no AI bear. I use AI every single day.

It saves me a shit ton of time and I’m not going back. It’s an incredible tool.

But market forces are still market forces.

Every boom in history has been overhyped, and every CEO wanted to stand up and tell Wall Street he could do more with half the people.

Now from what I’m seeing, reality is kicking in.

It costs way more than they thought, it breaks shit, and you still need people who know what the hell they’re doing.

Even the AI companies are feeling it. Elon just cut Grok’s usage limits and admitted it costs more to run than it brings in.

I still think AI is a great bet, and I’m still buying the companies building the data centers. But you need balance, and the guys who went all in on firing everyone are learning that the hard way.

Be careful out there.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
I'll only say this once.

Most investors will buy the WRONG stocks in November chasing momentum.

Here's my focus:

AVOID FOR NOW:
❌ $TSLA & $SPCX: Washington is coming for Elon

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Together they lost about $450B in two days.

Democrats now run Congress and are reportedly weighing probes into Musk's companies. Great businesses, but nobody knows how that fight ends. I'd wait.

Another one to avoid:

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
❌ Apple ( $AAPL ) - $344

The iPhone giant, and where everyone hid on Wednesday.

But China sales missed by $1B and Apple warned memory chip costs will squeeze its margins. Paying almost 40x earnings for that is a dangerous trade IMO.

Here's where I'm looking:

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Advanced Micro Devices ( $AMD ) - $404

Makes the AI chips that go head to head with Nvidia.

Data center sales nearly doubled last quarter to a record $8.5B. The stock still fell 17% on Thursday. This is a screaming buy IMO.

And the big tech name I'd own over Apple:

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Amazon ( $AMZN ) - $260

Runs the biggest cloud business in the world, and it's launching its own satellites to take on Starlink. It's worth about $2T less than Apple.

I think Amazon is a $4T company 12 months from now. It's in our portfolio for a reason.

And one more:

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Eaton ( $ETN ) - $327

Makes the gear that gets power into data centers. Its numbers held up, but the stock is now more than 30% off its high. The build-out is happening, it just takes years.

Here's why I'm getting bullish:

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
The S&P has gone up in the 12 months after EVERY midterm election since World War II.

A split government means less gets done in Washington, and markets love that.

Great companies are on sale right now, and you haven't heard me this bullish in three months.
